rows.derivation: The rule constrains an OPTIONAL implementor-defined '0x' letter status (A.1 item 106). COBOL.NET defines no letter status (FileStatusCode has none, per the adjudication), so the non-duplication constraint holds vacuously and the NOTE's case-equivalence cannot arise. No program can make the processor report a status it never produces, so nothing is observable beyond absence.
citations: cite.py --check 9.1.13.3 "This condition shall not duplicate any condition specified by another I-O status value" -> OK §9.1.13.3 1)
rows.notes: A golden asserting 'no 0x status' would pin an outcome every implementation without the optional feature shares. That is the latitude-without-observable case in WRITER.md step 6.

rows.derivation: Documented maximum 255 per run unit (CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-154), 15 per connector (DOC-A.1-155). Setup: 18 connectors on one 256-record relative file, SHARING WITH ALL OTHER, LOCK MODE MANUAL MULTIPLE. Connector i (1..17) locks distinct records (i-1)*15+1..i*15, so there is no '51' and no '54'. GRANTED=0255: all 255 locks are within the maximum. C18-256=53: C18 holds 0 locks and record 256 is unlocked, but the run unit holds the maximum, so item 3 gives '53'. C18-AGAIN=53: the failed READ obtained no lock. AFTER-CLOSE=00: CLOSE C01 releases 15 locks (§9.1.16), so the run unit holds 240 and the lock is granted.
citations: cite.py --check 9.1.13.8 "...this run unit holds the maximum number of locks allowed by this implementation" -> OK §9.1.13.8 3)
cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 "The implementor shall specify the maximum number of record locks" -> OK §12.4.5.9.4 7)
cite.py --check 9.1.16 "all record locks established for a file are released by the execution of an explicit or implicit CLOSE statement" -> OK §9.1.16
rows.notes: Pins the documented choice (255) itself: the 256th distinct lock on a connector below its own ceiling yields 53. The source is generated (18 SELECT/FD blocks) but checked in as plain COBOL.

rows.derivation: Both halves of the rule. (a) 'specified entirely on that line': '>>IF V =' with '1' on the next line must be rejected. It is, with COBOLNET1619 (malformed compile-time expression 'V ='). (b) 'shall begin on a new line': 'DISPLAY "A" >>IF V = 1' must be rejected. It is, with COBOL0307 unexpected '>'. The legal twins (the expression on one line; >>IF on its own line) compile and run.
citations: cite.py --check 7.3.16.3 "shall begin on a new line and shall be specified entirely on that line" -> OK §7.3.16.3 1)
cite.py --check 7.3.3 "A compiler directive shall be preceded only by zero, one, or more space characters" -> OK §7.3.3 2)
rows.notes: Rejected at 2002, 2014 and 2023. The mid-line .err is the generic parse code COBOL0307 ('unexpected '>''), which is allowed because this is a pure placement/syntax rule. The .err stops before the misleading 'A period may be missing' hint. COBOLNET1619 is the directive-expression-violation code, and its .err names the exact truncated operand 'V ='.

rows.derivation: Text-1 (DISPLAY "A") is written on the >>IF line after the expression, so text-1 does not begin on a new line and the source must be rejected. It is rejected with COBOLNET1619 malformed compile-time expression 'V = 1 DISPLAY...'. The legal twin (DISPLAY on the next line) runs and prints A.
citations: cite.py --check 7.3.16.3 "Text-1 shall begin on a new line" -> OK §7.3.16.3 2)
cite.py --check 7.3.3 "a compiler directive shall be written in the program-text area and may be followed only by space characters and an optional inline comment" -> OK §7.3.3 3)

rows.derivation: IF#1 is TRUE. Its eleven-line text-1 holds MOVE+DISPLAY, a >>DEFINE INNER AS 5, a nested >>IF/>>ELSE/>>END-IF, and a nested >>EVALUATE whose WHEN body is a two-line DISPLAY. GR2 includes all of it, giving A1 T1, A2 NESTED-IF and A3 NESTED-EVAL. Its text-2 (DISPLAY, >>DEFINE OUTER, nested IF) is omitted, so no BAD lines. IF#2 is FALSE. Its text-1 (>>DEFINE INNER AS 9 OVERRIDE plus two DISPLAYs) is omitted. Its four-line text-2 with a nested >>IF and a two-line DISPLAY is included, giving B1 TEXT2-FIRST and B2 TEXT2-NESTED. Directives in omitted text are not processed (§7.2.1 Step 2), so OUTER is not defined (OUTER-UNDEFINED, §7.3.8.4.4 GR2) and INNER is still 5 (INNER-IS-5).
citations: cite.py --check 7.3.16.3 "Text-1 and text-2 may consist of multiple lines" -> OK §7.3.16.3 6)
cite.py --check 7.3.16.4 "all lines of text-1 are included in the resultant text and all lines of text-2 are omitted" -> OK §7.3.16.4 2)
cite.py --check 7.3.16.4 "all lines of text-2 are included in the resultant text and all lines of text-1 are omitted from the resultant text" -> OK §7.3.16.4 3)
cite.py --check 7.2.1 "the expanded compilation group is read and the following compiler directives and substitutions are processed in the order encountered" -> OK §7.2.1
cite.py --check 7.3.8.4.4 "IS NOT DEFINED syntax evaluates TRUE if compilation-variable-name-1 is not currently defined" -> OK §7.3.8.4.4 2)
rows.notes: Closes the multiple-lines half that the refutation said pb1006 leaves unpinned. The compiler pads 'A1 T1' with trailing spaces (W is X(8)); the runner ignores them.

rows.derivation: INITIATE R-A R-B inside imperative-statement-1 of a Format-3 exception-checking PERFORM is the forbidden placement, so the source must be rejected. It is rejected with COBOLNET1605. The twin with two single-name INITIATEs compiles and runs.
citations: cite.py --check 14.9.21.3 "An INITIATE statement that specifies more than one report-name-1 shall not be specified in an exception checking PERFORM statement" -> OK §14.9.21.3 3)
rows.notes: reject-at 2023 only (Format-3 PERFORM is 2023-only). The .err is the code plus the message head. COBOLNET1605 is a raw code absent from docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md and DiagnosticCatalog (adjudicator hygiene note; not a defect of this rule).

rows.derivation: First, INITIATE R-A. Then INITIATE R-A R-B: the implicit INITIATE R-A raises EC-REPORT-ACTIVE (GR2), printing HANDLED (H=1). RESUME NEXT STATEMENT resumes at the implicit INITIATE R-B (GR5, the 'unless general rules ... specify otherwise' clause of §14.9.33.4 GR2a), so R-B is initiated, then AFTER-1 H=1. A second INITIATE R-A R-B with both reports active prints HANDLED twice (resume from the first goes to the second implicit INITIATE), then AFTER-2 H=3. GENERATE DET-B raises no EC-REPORT-INACTIVE because R-B is active, so there is no INACTIVE line. Read-back shows B-DETAIL. A wrong implementation that resumes at the next statement prints H=1/H=2 and INACTIVE.
citations: cite.py --check 14.9.21.4 "processing resumes at the next implicit INITIATE statement, if any" -> OK §14.9.21.4 5)
cite.py --check 14.9.21.4 "If it is in the active state, the EC-REPORT-ACTIVE exception condition is set to exist" -> OK §14.9.21.4 2)
cite.py --check 14.9.33.4 "unless general rules associated with the applicable statement specify otherwise" -> OK §14.9.33.4 2) a)
cite.py --check 14.9.16.4 "If it is not, the EC-REPORT-INACTIVE exception condition is set to exist" -> OK §14.9.16.4 7)
rows.notes: Placed in the 2023 directory because sentence 2 needs >>TURN, RESUME and the EC-REPORT-* declaratives. The sentence-1 ordering is shown by R-B being active after the resumed series. A 2002 twin was not written, so the 2002/2014 edition cells rest on this golden alone.
